item.title: Paraguay's ousted president charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
item.description: Prosecutors in Paraguay charged the South American nation’s recently deposed president with two crimes linked to the collapse of a major bank, that has jeopardized the savings of hundreds of thousands of account holders, and unleashed the nation’s biggest political crisis in a decade.

item.title: Polish gunman who killed 6 people in Krakow has 'ultranationalistic' views, authorities say
item.description: A Polish man who authorities say harbors far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow and opened fire, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him.

item.title: Nithya Raman to take charge in LA amid homeless crisis and political division
item.description: In her bid for Los Angeles mayor, Nithya Raman ran as an outsider. The democratic socialist didn’t win a single endorsement from her 14 colleagues on the city council.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway buys back $9.6 billion of its own stock but its profits declined
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway repurchased $9.6 billion worth of its own stock in the third quarter, but Geico's numbers worsened and its overall profit fell more than 28% as the value of its investments changed.
